intro: The Torah is a very long scroll. Its first book is called Bereshit. That means "In the beginning." This unit tells the first stories in that book. You will hear about the very first week, a day of rest, a garden, a big boat, a dove and a rainbow.

Jewish families have read these stories for a very long time. Many families in Chicago read them every year. In this unit we learn what the Torah says. We learn what the stories mean to the people who read them. We do not decide if they are true. We listen and we learn.

By the end, you will be able to tell the story of the first week. You will know what Shabbat is. You will be able to tell the story of Noah, the ark and the rainbow. And you will know what a promise is.
bigQuestion: What do the first stories in the Torah say about the world, rest and promises?

title: In the Beginning

chapters.title: Seven Days and Shabbat
chapters.bigQuestion: What does the first story in the Torah say happened in the very first week?

story.title: Two Candles on Friday Night
story.kicker: The sun goes down, two candles are lit, and a family hears the story of the very first week.
paragraphs: It is Friday night at Maya's house in Chicago. The sun is going down. Her mom lights two candles on the table. Maya's dad puts a cloth over a braided bread. The bread is called challah. It smells warm and sweet.
Maya's grandpa opens a big book. He says, "This is the story of the first week." He reads slowly. "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth." Maya listens. The candles flicker.

Grandpa reads about light, sky, land and sea. He reads about sun, moon and stars. He reads about fish, birds, animals and people. Then he reads about the seventh day. "On that day," he says, "the story says God rested."

Maya's family calls this day Shabbat. It is a day of rest. They eat, they sing, and they do not rush. Maya asks, "Is this the same story every week?" Grandpa smiles. "Yes," he says. "And every week it feels new."
story.think: Why do you think Maya's family lights candles before they tell the story of the first week?

sections.title: The Torah and Its First Book

lessons.title: A Scroll with Five Books
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah is a long scroll with five books inside it.
reading: The *Torah* is a very long scroll. A scroll is a roll of paper or animal skin. You do not turn pages. You roll it open. The Torah is kept in a special place in a synagogue. A synagogue is where Jewish people pray and learn.
The Torah has five books inside it. Five, like the fingers on one hand. Jewish tradition says all five books belong together. The first book tells the very first stories.
Every week, Jewish people read one part of the Torah. It takes one whole year to read it all. Then they start again from the beginning.

words.d: the first five books of the Hebrew Bible, kept as one long scroll
a long roll of paper or animal skin with writing on it

look.title: Counting the Torah
look.cite: Jewish tradition; the five books are Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy
look.prompt: How many books are in the Torah? Hold up that many fingers.

check.q: How many books are in the Torah?
check.why: The Torah has five books. That is why people sometimes call it the Five Books of Moses.

check.q: What is a scroll?
choices: A roll of paper or skin with writing on it
A book with a hard cover
check.why: A scroll is rolled open, not turned page by page. The Torah is a scroll.

check.q: How long does it take to read the whole Torah in a synagogue?
check.why: Jewish people read one part each week. It takes a whole year to finish.

lessons.title: In the Beginning
lessons.mainIdea: The first book of the Torah is called Bereshit, which means "In the beginning."
reading: The first book of the Torah has a Hebrew name. It is *Bereshit*. Bereshit means "In the beginning." That is the very first word of the book. In English, the book is called Genesis.
The Torah is written in Hebrew. Hebrew is read from right to left. The first line says, "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth." That is how the Torah starts.
When people talk about this book, they say "the Torah says." Jewish tradition reads it as a holy book. In school, we learn what the story says and what it means to the people who read it.

words.d: the Hebrew name of the first book of the Torah; it means "In the beginning"
the English name for Bereshit, the first book of the Torah

look.title: The First Line
look.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
look.prompt: What two big things does this first line say were made?

check.q: What does Bereshit mean?
check.why: Bereshit is the first word of the Torah. It means "In the beginning."

check.q: What is the English name for the book called Bereshit?
check.why: Genesis is the English name. Bereshit is the Hebrew name for the same book.

check.q: Which way is Hebrew read?
check.why: Hebrew is read from right to left. English is read the other way.

lessons.title: Light, Sky, Land and Sea
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says the first three days brought light, sky, land and sea.
reading: The Torah tells the story of the first week. On day one, the story says, God said, "Let there be light." And there was *light*. God called the light Day. God called the dark Night.
On day two, the story says God made the sky. The sky is like a big roof over the world. On day three, the story says God made dry land and the sea. Then plants grew. Grass, trees and fruit.
After each day, the story says, God saw that it was good. Jewish tradition reads this as a big "yes" to the world.

words.d: the first thing the Torah says God made; God called it Day

look.title: Let There Be Light
look.text: And God said: 'Let there be light.' And there was light.
look.prompt: Close your eyes. Now open them. What do you see because of light?

check.q: What does the Torah say was made on day one?
check.why: On day one, the story says, God said, "Let there be light."

check.q: What does the Torah say was made on day three?
choices: Dry land, the sea and plants
check.why: Day three brought land, sea and plants. The sun and moon come on day four.

check.q: What did God call the light, in the story?
check.why: The story says God called the light Day and the dark Night.

lessons.title: Sun, Moon and Stars
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says the sun, moon and stars were made on day four.
reading: On day four, the story says, God made two big lights. One big light rules the day. That is the *sun*. One smaller light rules the night. That is the moon. The story says God made the stars too.
The Torah says these lights are for signs and seasons. They mark days and years. Jewish families use the moon to count their months. A new moon starts a new month.

words.d: the big light for the day; the Torah says it was made on day four
the light for the night; Jewish months start with a new moon

look.title: Day and Night
look.text: Picture the sky at noon. The sun is high and bright. Now picture the sky at night. The moon is out. Small stars twinkle. The Torah says the big light is for the day and the small light is for the night.
look.prompt: Which light do you see right now? Is it day or night?

check.q: In the story, which light rules the day?
check.why: The Torah says the big light, the sun, rules the day.

check.q: On which day does the story say the sun and moon were made?
check.why: Day four brought the sun, the moon and the stars in the Torah's story.

check.q: What starts a new Jewish month?
check.why: Jewish months follow the moon. A new moon starts a new month.

lessons.title: Fish, Birds, Animals and People
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says living things came on days five and six, and people came last.
reading: On day five, the story says, God made the fish in the sea. God made the *birds* in the sky. The water was full. The air was full. The story says God blessed them.

On day six, the story says God made the animals on the land. Cows, bugs, lions, all of them. Then, last of all, God made people. The Torah says people were made in God's image. Jewish tradition reads this as: every person matters.
At the end of day six, the story says God looked at everything. And it was very good.

words.d: the animals of the sky; the Torah says they were made on day five with the fish
a likeness; the Torah says people were made in God's image

look.title: The Six Days
rows: Days for light, sky, land and sea
Day for sun, moon and stars
Days for fish, birds, animals and people
look.prompt: Add up the days. How many days of making are there?

check.q: What does the Torah say was made on day five?
check.why: Day five brought fish and birds. Land animals and people came on day six.

check.q: Who does the story say was made last of all?
check.why: People were made last, at the end of day six.

check.q: How does Jewish tradition read "made in God's image"?
check.why: Jewish tradition reads this as: every person is important.

lessons.title: A Day of Rest
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says God rested on the seventh day, and Jewish families call that day Shabbat.
reading: On the seventh day, the story says, God stopped. The work was done. God rested. The Torah says God blessed the seventh day and made it holy. Holy means set apart and special.

Jewish families call the seventh day *Shabbat*. It starts on Friday night when the sun goes down. It ends on Saturday night. On Shabbat, many Jewish families do not work. They rest, eat and sing together.
Two candles are lit. A cup of grape juice or wine is blessed. There is braided bread called challah. The rest is the point. Jewish tradition says Shabbat is a gift.

words.d: the seventh day of the week, a day of rest for Jewish families, from Friday night to Saturday night
set apart and special

look.title: The Seventh Day
look.text: The Torah says that on the seventh day God finished the work and rested. Then God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it God rested from all the work of making.
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 2:2–3, paraphrased from the Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: What did God do on the seventh day, in the story?

check.q: What does the Torah say God did on the seventh day?
check.why: The story says the work was done. God rested on the seventh day.

check.q: What do Jewish families call the seventh day?
check.why: Shabbat is the Jewish day of rest. Bereshit and Genesis are names of a book.

check.q: When does Shabbat start?
check.why: Shabbat starts Friday night when the sun goes down. It ends Saturday night.

lessons.title: Candles, Bread and Songs
lessons.mainIdea: Jewish families welcome Shabbat with candles, bread and songs.
reading: On Friday night, many Jewish families light two candles. They say a blessing. A blessing is a short thank-you prayer. The candles say: Shabbat is here.
There is a braided bread called *challah*. Often there are two loaves. Families say a blessing over the bread and share it. They eat a big meal. They sing songs.
Not every Jewish family keeps Shabbat the same way. Some go to a synagogue. Some take a quiet walk. Some play games. All of them are resting from the week.

words.d: a braided bread that Jewish families eat on Shabbat
a short thank-you prayer

look.title: A Shabbat Table
look.cite: Common Jewish Shabbat practice, as many families keep it
look.prompt: What is on a Shabbat table? Count the things in the list.

check.q: How many candles do many families light for Shabbat?
check.why: Two candles are lit on Friday night to welcome Shabbat.

check.q: What is challah?
check.why: Challah is the braided bread that families eat on Shabbat.

check.q: Do all Jewish families keep Shabbat the same way?
choices: No, families keep it in different ways
check.why: Families keep Shabbat in many ways. Some pray, some walk, some play. All rest.

lessons.title: A Garden Called Eden
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah tells of a garden called Eden with trees, rivers and the first people.
reading: The Torah tells of a garden. The garden is called *Eden*. It has many trees with good fruit. It has a river that runs through it. The story says God put the first people there.
The first man is called Adam. The woman is called Eve. In Hebrew her name is Chava. Their job was to care for the garden. The Torah says God gave them one rule about one tree.
The story says they ate from that tree. Then they had to leave the garden. Jewish tradition tells this story in many ways. In school, we read what the story says.

words.d: the garden in the Torah where the first people lived
the first man in the Torah's story

look.title: Walk Through the Garden
look.text: Picture a garden. Tall trees hold red and yellow fruit. A river runs through the middle. Birds sing. Two people walk on the soft grass. They have a job: to care for this place.
look.prompt: If you had a garden to care for, what would you do first?

check.q: What is Eden?
choices: A garden in the Torah's story
check.why: Eden is the garden where the Torah says the first people lived.

check.q: What was the first people's job in the garden?
check.why: The Torah says the people were put in the garden to care for it.

check.q: What is Eve's name in Hebrew?
check.why: Chava is the Hebrew name for Eve. Sarah and Miriam are other people in the Torah.

review.why: The Torah is a long scroll. It has five books inside it.

review.q: What is the Hebrew name of the first book of the Torah?
review.why: Bereshit means "In the beginning." In English it is called Genesis.

review.q: How many days of making are in the story?
review.why: The story has six days of making. On the seventh day, God rested.

review.q: What does the Torah say was made first?
review.why: Light was made on day one. People came last, on day six.

review.q: What do Jewish families do on Shabbat?
review.why: Shabbat is a day of rest. Families eat, sing and rest together.

review.q: Where does the Torah say the first people lived?
review.why: The Torah says the first people lived in the garden of Eden.

chapters.title: Noah, the Ark and the Rainbow
chapters.bigQuestion: What does the Torah say a promise is, and how did Noah's family learn about one?

story.title: A Leaf in Her Beak
story.kicker: After many days of rain and waiting, a small bird flies home with big news.
paragraphs: Rain, rain, rain. In the Torah's story, Noah's family sat inside a very big boat. The boat was full of animals. Sheep bleated. Doves cooed. Lions yawned. Outside, water covered everything. There was no land to see.
One day the rain stopped. Noah opened a window. He let a dove fly out. The dove flew and flew. She found no place to land. She came back tired. Noah put out his hand and took her in.

Seven days later, Noah sent the dove out again. Everyone waited. Then, near evening, a small shape came through the sky. It was the dove. In her beak was a fresh green leaf. An olive leaf! Somewhere, a tree was growing.

Everyone on the boat cheered. The water was going down. Soon they would walk on dry land again. The Torah's story says the dove went out one more time. That time, she did not come back. She had found a home.
story.think: Why did everyone cheer when they saw the leaf? What did the leaf tell them?

lessons.title: Noah Builds an Ark
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says God told Noah to build a very big boat called an ark.
reading: The Torah tells about a man named *Noah*. The story says the world was full of bad ways. But Noah was good. The Torah says God told Noah that a big flood was coming.
God told Noah to build an *ark*. An ark is a very big boat. Noah made it from wood. He covered it inside and out so water could not get in. It had a door on the side and a window on top.
The ark had three floors. It was very long. It took Noah a long time to build. His three sons helped. Their names were Shem, Ham and Japheth.

words.d: the man in the Torah who built the ark
the very big boat that Noah built in the Torah's story

look.title: How Big Was the Ark?
look.prompt: Which number is the biggest? Was the ark longer or taller?

check.q: What is an ark?
check.why: In the Torah's story, the ark is the very big boat Noah built.

check.q: Why does the Torah say Noah built the ark?
check.why: The story says God told Noah a flood was coming, so Noah built the ark.

check.q: How many floors did the ark have, in the story?
check.why: The Torah says the ark had three floors: a bottom, a middle and a top.

lessons.title: Two by Two
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says the animals came into the ark two by two.
reading: The story says the animals came to the ark. They came in *pairs*. A pair is two. One boy and one girl of each kind. Birds, cows, snakes, bugs. Some kinds came in bigger groups of seven pairs.
Noah's family went in too. Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives. That is eight people. Then, the story says, God closed the door.
Picture the line of animals. Two giraffes with long necks. Two mice with tiny feet. Two elephants stomping up the ramp. That is how many children picture it.

words.d: two of something that go together

look.title: Line Up the Animals
look.text: Look at the line going up the ramp. Two ducks waddle. Two horses trot. Two turtles go very, very slowly. Behind them, two frogs hop. The Torah's story says they came two by two, a boy and a girl of each kind.
look.prompt: Pick an animal. Say its name two times, one for each in the pair.

check.q: How does the Torah say the animals came into the ark?
check.why: The story says the animals came two by two, a pair of each kind.

check.q: What is a pair?
check.why: A pair is two things that go together, like two shoes.

check.q: How many people does the Torah say went into the ark?
check.why: Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives make eight people.

lessons.title: Forty Days of Rain
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says it rained for forty days and forty nights.
reading: The Torah says the rain began. It rained for *forty* days and forty nights. Forty is a lot of days. It is more than a month. Water covered the land. Water covered even the hills.
The ark floated on top of the water. Inside, Noah's family fed the animals. They waited. The Torah says God remembered Noah. Then a wind blew, and the water started to go down.
The ark came to rest on a mountain. The mountains of Ararat, the Torah says. But the water was still high. Noah had to wait some more.

words.d: the number 40; the Torah says the rain lasted forty days and forty nights
water that covers the land

look.title: Counting the Days
rows: Days Noah waited before sending the dove again
Times the dove was sent out
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 7:12 and 8:8–12, Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Which number is the biggest? Which is the smallest?

check.q: How long does the Torah say it rained?
check.why: The Torah says it rained forty days and forty nights.

check.q: What is a flood?
check.why: A flood is water that covers the land. In the story, it covered the hills.

check.q: Where does the Torah say the ark came to rest?
check.why: The Torah says the ark rested on the mountains of Ararat.

lessons.title: The Dove and the Leaf
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says a dove brought back an olive leaf, a sign that the water was going down.
reading: Noah wanted to know if the land was dry. He sent out a raven first. Then he sent a *dove*. A dove is a soft gray or white bird. The first time, the dove found no place to land. She came back.
Noah waited seven days. He sent the dove again. This time she came back with an *olive leaf* in her beak. Now Noah knew. Trees were growing. The water was going down.
Seven more days. Noah sent the dove one more time. She did not come back. Then Noah opened the ark, and the story says God told the family to come out.

words.d: a soft gray or white bird; in the Torah's story it brought Noah an olive leaf
a small green leaf from an olive tree; a sign that land was near

look.title: The Dove Comes Home
look.text: The Torah says the dove came back to Noah in the evening. In her mouth was an olive leaf, freshly picked. So Noah knew that the water had gone down from the earth.
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 8:11, paraphrased from the Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: How did the leaf tell Noah the water was going down?

check.q: What did the dove bring back?
check.why: The dove brought back an olive leaf. It was a sign that trees were growing.

check.q: Which bird did Noah send out first?
check.why: The Torah says Noah sent a raven first, then the dove.

check.q: What did the leaf tell Noah?
check.why: A leaf means a tree was growing on dry ground. The water was going down.

lessons.title: The Rainbow Promise
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says the rainbow is a sign of God's promise never to flood the whole world again.
reading: When the ground was dry, everyone came out of the ark. The animals ran and flew. The Torah says Noah said thank you to God. Then God made a *promise*. God said there would never again be a flood over all the earth.
The story says God put a *rainbow* in the clouds. The rainbow is a sign. It is like a reminder. When people see a rainbow, they can remember the promise.
Jewish tradition has a blessing for seeing a rainbow. It thanks God for remembering the promise. A promise is something you say you will do. And then you do it.

words.d: something you say you will do, and then you do it
the bow of colors in the sky; the Torah says it is a sign of God's promise

look.title: A Bow in the Cloud
look.text: The Torah says God set a bow in the cloud. It would be a sign of the promise between God and the earth.
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 9:13, paraphrased from the Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: What is the rainbow a sign of, in the story?

check.q: What does the Torah say the rainbow is?
check.why: The story says the rainbow is a sign of God's promise never to flood the whole earth again.

check.q: What is a promise?
choices: Something you say you will do, and then do
check.why: A promise is a thing you say you will do. Keeping it means doing it.

check.q: What does Jewish tradition say when someone sees a rainbow?
choices: A blessing that remembers the promise
check.why: Jewish tradition has a blessing for a rainbow. It remembers God's promise.

lessons.title: The Tower of Babel
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says people built a tall tower, and then they began to speak many languages.
reading: After the flood, the Torah says, everyone spoke one *language*. A language is the words people use to talk. The people came to a flat land. They said, "Let us build a city and a tower up to the sky."
They made bricks. They built and built. The story says God came down to see the tower. Then God mixed up their words. They could not understand each other. They stopped building.
The people spread out over the earth. The place was called *Babel*. Jewish tradition reads this story as a lesson. Some rabbis say the people cared more about the tower than about each other.

words.d: the words people use to talk to each other
the place in the Torah where people built a tower and began to speak many languages

look.title: Who Can Understand?
look.text: Picture a big building site. One worker says, "Pass me a brick," in one language. The next worker hears sounds she does not know. She hands him a jug of water instead. Nobody can plan together anymore.
look.prompt: What happens to a big job when people cannot understand each other?

check.q: What did the people at Babel try to build?
choices: A tower up to the sky
check.why: The Torah says the people tried to build a city and a tower up to the sky.

check.q: What is a language?
choices: The words people use to talk
check.why: A language is the set of words people use to talk to each other.

check.q: Why did the people stop building, in the story?
choices: They could not understand each other
check.why: The Torah says their words were mixed up. They could not understand each other.

lessons.title: One Story, Many Families
lessons.mainIdea: Jews, Christians and Muslims all tell a story of Noah, and each reads it in its own way.
reading: Noah's story is in the Torah. Jewish families read it in the synagogue every fall. *Christians* read the same story in their Bible. Many Christian churches in Chicago tell it to children too.
*Muslims* tell a story of Noah too. In Arabic, his name is Nuh. The Qur'an, the holy book of Islam, has a chapter named after him. It tells how Nuh warned people and built a boat.
Each tradition reads the story in its own way. But all three tell of a good man, a big boat and a promise. You may hear it in a synagogue, a church or a mosque.

words.d: people who follow Christianity; they read Noah's story in their Bible
people who follow Islam; their holy book, the Qur'an, tells of Noah, called Nuh

check.q: Which three traditions in this lesson tell a story of Noah?
check.why: Jews, Christians and Muslims all tell a story of Noah, each in its own way.

check.why: Christians read Noah's story in their Bible, and many churches tell it to children.

review.q: What did Noah build, in the Torah's story?
review.why: Noah built an ark, a very big boat, because a flood was coming.

review.q: How did the animals come into the ark?
review.why: The Torah says the animals came two by two, a pair of each kind.

review.q: How many days did it rain?
review.why: The Torah says it rained for forty days and forty nights.

review.q: What did the dove bring back to the ark?
review.why: The dove brought an olive leaf. It showed the water was going down.

review.q: What does the Torah say the rainbow means?

review.q: What happened at Babel, in the story?

review.why: At Babel, the Torah says, the people's words were mixed up into many languages.
